limitations: Published receipts require separate local byte-for-byte qualification before exactness is claimed
Body bytes exclude HTTP headers, TLS, TCP/IP and tunnel overhead; packet evidence is joined separately
Failed rows contain attempted upload body bytes and completely received response bodies, not proven link bytes
No WAN speed claim follows from running this summarizer
Break-even extrapolates constant per-transfer savings; it is not a measured sequence
Receiver process CPU excludes relay/cloudflared and socket wait; sender CPU includes HTTP/TLS
Failed pairs remain in receipts but are excluded from ratios; inspect failures before interpreting success-only statistics
Each suite requires a fresh isolated receiver cache; suites are not combined under one cache quota
Application cache state is controlled; OS page/disk caches are not flushed
The DAG arm uses the current executable's full-fold path, not the historical pre-optimization binary
Prepared base construction is charged inside the seed timer; the same owned state survives into its immediately following transfer
Prepared target comparison/hash/closure work and terminal retained-state teardown are timed; this one-update experiment performs no successor promotion
Resident charges are conservative owned-state accounting, not process RSS or preparation peak memory; shared graphs may be counted twice
Sparse encoding, comparison and fallback selection are timed; sparse is an aligned/prefix/suffix recipe, not content-defined chunking
Repeat full-copy controls have empty target scopes; raw-CAS, DAG, prepared and sparse share the general object-cache shortcut
Localized edits change 32 bytes; scattered edits change 1024 bytes, not an equal edit budget
Transfer timing starts with generated in-memory inputs before graph/codec preparation; fixture generation is measured separately
Arms use seeded cyclic counterbalanced paired order, not an independent random shuffle or balanced carryover design
Begin cache hits are valid only for seeded repeat targets; hits during seeds or modified-target uploads invalidate those operations
Receiver CPU covers decode/handle/encode; relay/cloudflared CPU and socket wait are excluded; CPU is not an energy measurement
HTTP body counts are not packet/link bytes; failed-upload counts are attempted body bytes
quantiles: nearest rank: sorted[ceil(n*p)-1], including lower middle for even-n median
